native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: PC1 of the forms of capital starts the Younger Bronze Age at its global maximum at 1100 BCE and is substantially higher than at every subsequent hundred-year horizon (differences +2.28 to +3.64), declining to about one-fifth of its peak by 500 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (German decimal commas; 39x12, no missing). Ran SVD PCA on the full 39x12 matrix (Z-scored variables, covariance==correlation); kept natural sign (+ = accumulation; 31.8% variance). Extracted PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.45, global max) and at 1000–500 BCE; computed per-horizon differences PC1(1100)-PC1(t), mean of 1000–500 (+1.44), and in-period trend (r=+0.86 in BCE space, i.e., decline over time). Reported YBA-only PCA as a sensitivity that inverts polarity. Saved scores CSV and stats JSON.
